verdict.root_cause: At 09:00:04, ~3 minutes before onset, platform automation attached a traffic-shaping container to cartservice's network namespace imposing a fixed 300ms zero-jitter egress delay on eth0 [tr_453388522751]. From ~09:04 every cartservice Redis round trip sits at a near-constant ~300-310ms against a sub-millisecond baseline, while the gRPC handler's own self-time stays ~1ms, and callers absorb integer multiples of the same quantum [tr_00648f14b2cc]. That propagation explains why checkoutservice, frontend and loadgenerator alerted seconds later while still completing orders successfully, only with per-step gaps stretched to ~1.2s [tr_2e9a61da7944]. cartservice serves continuously with no error or restart text [tr_d973409279b4]. The mechanism is waiting on a deliberately slowed call path; the fix is detaching the shaping container.
verdict.reasoning: The change record's injected 300ms zero-jitter delay and the traces' constant ~300-310ms floor per Redis operation are two independent sources agreeing on the same number [tr_453388522751][tr_00648f14b2cc]. The fixed-quantum signature, identical across HGET/HMSET and across callers including parentless orphan traces, rules out cache contention or load-driven scaling. Handler self-time of ~1ms places the cost in the round trip, not in code. Downstream alerts follow mechanically: checkout logs are info-only with successful payments and advancing queue offsets, just slower [tr_2e9a61da7944]. The hotfix image was reverted ~12 minutes before onset, so no new artifact was live [tr_453388522751]. I chose dependency_latency over bad_config because no value names a wrong target; delay was inserted into the path and the waiting is the failure.
open_questions: checkoutservice's only error change point is 08:43:30, ~17 minutes BEFORE the delay was attached [tr_5902e13a22c6][tr_453388522751] — the injected latency cannot explain an error onset that predates it, and errors did not clear after the 08:51 image revert.
Both log results are truncated, leaving 08:33:39-09:04:19 unreturned [tr_d973409279b4][tr_2e9a61da7944]; the 08:43 onset and any error burst or brief restart in that gap are unexamined.
cartservice has no metric samples in either window [tr_ce171ca4b48c], so its request rate, latency, restarts and saturation are entirely unmeasured.

alternatives.root_cause: An earlier, still-unidentified fault at ~08:43 drives checkoutservice's error ratio, with the 09:00 delay injection a separate later event that only worsened latency.
alternatives.why_not: The 08:43 change point is real and unexplained, but no specialist found any error mechanism — no aborts in traces, no error-severity logs — so this names a timing gap rather than a fault; the latency symptom that triggered the alerts is fully accounted for by the delay injection.

alternatives.root_cause: The cartservice hotfix image applied ~08:42 introduced errors that persisted past its 08:51 revert.
alternatives.why_not: The image was already reverted 12 minutes before onset, so the pre-hotfix artifact was running when symptoms began [tr_453388522751], and a reverted image should not sustain an elevated error ratio through the end of the window.

proposal.expected_effect: No action proposed. The delay lives in a separate traffic-shaping container attached to cartservice's network namespace (eth0 delay=300ms jitter=0ms) [tr_453388522751], not in cartservice's own image or environment; no permitted action detaches it. revert_config fails its precondition - change history records only two image events and one container attachment, no config or env edit [tr_453388522751]. rollback_image is ruled out because the only image change was already reverted before onset [tr_453388522751]. restart_service is not indicated: cartservice serves continuously with ~1ms handler self-time and no error or restart text, so process state is not the fault [tr_00648f14b2cc]. If an operator detaches the shaper out of band, the check is Tempo: cartservice Redis HGET/HMSET child spans back from ~300-310ms to ~0.2ms, checkout traces from ~2.47s toward ~27ms.
proposal.if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if change history on re-read holds a prior cartservice configuration that revert_config would restore, or if recreating the container is confirmed to drop the shaper's namespace attachment - either makes a config_revert legal rather than speculative. It is vindicated if a revert is attempted and Redis child spans stay pinned at ~300ms.
proposal.risk: Abstaining leaves the ~300ms floor in place: checkout stays near 2.5s per order and the four alerts keep firing. It also leaves unaddressed checkoutservice's separate error onset at 08:43:30, which predates the shaper by ~17 minutes and did not clear after the 08:51 image revert [tr_5902e13a22c6] - no permitted action targets that mechanism, and cartservice has zero metric samples in either window, so any action's effect would be unmeasurable on that service.
proposal.blast_radius: No change, so nobody sees a state transition. Continuing impact is borne by cartservice's callers named in the brief - checkoutservice, frontend and loadgenerator - which keep completing orders at ~1.2s per step.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Multiple services alerting within seconds starting at cartservice and fanning through checkoutservice and frontend is a propagating failure, not a single quiet warning. Cart being first suggests a downstream dependency or its datastore degrading.
